source_instruction: i  need fluoide free toothpaste for fresh breath.
query: I stopped by the community garden on my walk home yesterday and spent nearly 40 minutes chatting with the retired guy who tends the tomato beds by the fence. He brought out a jar of the sun-warmed cherry tomatoes he’d picked that morning to pass around to everyone lingering nearby, and they were so sweet they tasted like they’d been dipped in a little sugar, no extra prep needed at all. A group of tiny kids from the daycare down the block came trotting through right as I was leaving, each clutching a crumpled dandelion they’d picked along the path, and their teacher was laughing so hard she could barely corral them when one of the kids tried to tuck a dandelion behind her ear. I’ve heard there’s toothpaste that helps keep breath smelling fresh all day. I’ve heard that option doesn’t land too high on what people shell out for it, so it stays light on the wallet. I’ve heard it’s got none of that stuff people usually skip when they’re looking at natural toothpaste.
